column1: # Game profile of Hello Kitty Party Land (Switch, update 1.0.2 = v131072). Plays on the Mac and on the iPhone at 60 fps
# Unity 6000.3.11f1 (IL2CPP) with CRIWARE movies (USM) and Addressables, SDK 21.4.4; subsdk0 is the movie module. The player's serialized files and built-in resources have no type trees; the
# Shader objects borrow the tree the Addressables bundles carry, and the ComputeShader objects (Unity's GPU skinning among them) take unityfs.py's written-out 6000.3 layout (COMPUTE_6000_3).
# The game runs its menus at 60 fps and switches gameplay to 30; patches.py keeps its own 60 fps mode everywhere (README.md, Frame rate)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true, and main never sets a heap: Unity 6 takes its memory itself in the alias region, as in BALL x PIT and
# Hollow Knight: Silksong. The 5 GB block of the other Unity games with virtual address memory. Measured on the Mac (2026-11-01, menus, the tutorial and minigames): the alias region's
# high-water mark +2.75 GB of 4.375 GB, 1.26 GB mapped, about 2 GB resident and 0.5 GB of GPU memory
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader and ComputeShader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles (12,739 shaders, 92 of them compute, 11 GLSLC outputs of Unity's player in main)
